title: Bhindi Masala (Jain)
subtitle: Okra sautéed until dry, then folded into a jammy tomato-cashew masala with amchur and kasuri methi.
protein: ~3g protein per adult serving (low — pair with dal, dahi or paneer)

method.title: Dry and sauté the okra
items: Wash {@okra} and spread on a clean towel; let it dry fully, at least 20 min — moisture is what makes it slimy
Trim stems and tips; cut into 1-inch pieces
Heat {@oil} in a wide kadai on medium-high; add the pieces in a single layer (two batches if crowded)
Sauté uncovered {10 min}, stirring often, until the sticky strings disappear and the edges are lightly browned
Set aside on a plate; keep the same pan

method.title: Tomato masala
items: Heat {@ghee} in the same pan on medium
Add {@tomatoes} and {@cashew-powder}; cook uncovered {8 min}, mashing, until jammy and the ghee separates (splash in water {2–3 tbsp} if it sticks)

method.label: Toddler — pull portion here (before chili and garam masala)
items: Scoop out the masala {3–4 tbsp} into a small pan
Cut {@okra:toddler|her share of the sautéed okra} small and add it with {@salt:toddler}
Cover and cook on low {3 min} until soft
Optional: stir in {@potato:toddler|finely diced boiled potato} for extra bulk

method.title: Finish the adult masala
items: Add {@chili-powder} and {@garam-masala} to the main pan; cook {30 sec} on low
Return {@okra:main|the remaining sautéed okra}; fold gently so it doesn't mash
Add {@amchur} and {@kasuri-methi}; cook uncovered on low {3 min} until the masala clings
Garnish with {@coriander-leaves}; cool and refrigerate up to 3 days, reheating in a pan

method.label: Tip
method.text: Keep okra away from steam: dry it fully, sauté it before it meets the tomatoes, and keep the pan uncovered. onion → tomato cooked until jammy + cashew powder + hing, so the masala needs no extra thickener.
